overview.headline: Ground Penetrating Radar Survey in Kenya
paragraphs: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) surveys use electromagnetic pulses to detect and map buried utilities, voids, rebar, and subsurface anomalies without excavation. GPR is the primary tool for pre-excavation utility mapping, concrete scanning, and void detection across construction sites in Nairobi and beyond.
SmartGrid Surveying uses GSSI-class GPR systems with experienced operators, delivering same-day preliminary findings and detailed reports with CAD-ready drawings.

Searching for a ground penetrating radar survey near you? Our GPR teams are based in Nairobi and dispatch across Kenya — Kiambu, Nakuru, Kisumu, Mombasa — with most requests mobilized within 24 hours.

limitations.headline: Technical Limitations (Transparency You Can Trust)
limitations.description: Ground Penetrating Radar performance depends on site conditions. We tell you exactly what to expect:

items.title: Clay Soils
items.description: Heavy clay attenuates the radar signal and reduces effective penetration depth.

items.title: Dense Reinforcement
items.description: Concentrated rebar and mesh cause signal scattering and clutter inside concrete.

items.title: Wet Ground
items.description: High soil moisture changes the dielectric response and can mask target signatures.

items.title: Maximum Effective Depth
items.description: Typical detection depth varies between 0.5m – 4m depending on soil and antenna configuration.

limitations.note: We combine GPR with EM locating & site verification to improve reliability.

items.question: What is a GPR survey?
items.answer: A GPR (Ground Penetrating Radar) survey uses electromagnetic pulses fired into the ground to locate buried utilities, rebar, voids, and other subsurface features without excavation or drilling. The radar unit is pushed across the surface and the reflected signals are processed into a map showing the depth and position of detected features.

items.question: How deep can GPR detect in Kenyan soil conditions?
items.answer: Detection depth depends on soil type. In sandy or volcanic soils we typically achieve 3-8 meters of penetration, while wet clay heavily attenuates the signal and may limit depth to 1-2 meters. Where deeper targets are expected, we deploy lower-frequency antennas and combine GPR with electromagnetic locators.

items.question: Can GPR work through concrete?
items.answer: Yes. Concrete scanning is one of the most common GPR applications — we locate rebar, post-tension cables, conduits, and voids within slabs, walls, and beams quickly and without any damage to the structure.

items.question: Do you provide same-day results?
items.answer: Preliminary findings and on-site markouts are provided immediately after scanning. Full interpreted reports and CAD drawings are delivered within the timeline agreed for your project — typically a few days depending on site size.

items.question: Is GPR safe to use indoors?
items.answer: Completely safe. GPR emits low-power radio waves — there is no radiation risk to people, and the method is entirely non-destructive, making it ideal for occupied buildings, hospitals, and live industrial facilities.
